market_view: The AI-capex selloff deepened Friday: the S&P 500 fell 1.82% to 7,580, the Nasdaq fell 2.86% (7.8% off its Oct 6 high), chips fell 7.2% and VIX rose to 19.4, while energy (oil ~$104) and some health care held up (Reuters, Oct 30). Monday's pre-open prints (IDXX, CHKP) and Apple/Palantir after the close, Tuesday's midterms and AMD, and Friday's payrolls make this a week of binary events, so I'm adding only one defensive, non-AI compounder and no short-term trades.
lessons: My non-AI compounders keep working while the AI-capex ones fail: LLY is +8.5% and BLK +0.8% versus GOOGL (-17.7%, stop) and AMZN (-9.5%, sold), and on Friday LLY rose 3.2% while the Nasdaq fell 2.86% (compounder n=4, a hunch). So I'm filling one free slot with AbbVie, which hit a record on a down-1.8% day, and still adding no AI-capex name.

I'm still losing to the market: the evidence table puts my alpha at -1.14% per trade over 81 trades (95% range -2.11% to -0.18%, a 2.8% chance of beating random) versus about 0% for the Fruit Fly and -0.93% for Momentum, and moonshots remain my weakest book (n=40, 15% win rate). So I submit zero moonshots again; Monday's only fresh catalysts are pre-open prints I can't see.

Per the instruction to keep stops outside 1.5x the daily range, I checked Okta's S&P 500 add (effective Nov 4, +2.1% after hours after a -6.1% day): its daily range has run 5-7%, so a sane stop is ~10% and a 1.5:1 target would need +15% in two sessions, which is unrealistic. The lab also shows first sessions that open up 2%+ losing -5.4% open-to-close (n=16, a hunch), so I pass instead of forcing it.

review.reason: It fell 1.55% to $521.91 Friday with the Nasdaq (-2.86%) on sector-wide AI-capex worries, not company news; the 48% Azure beat thesis is intact and the $495 stop sits ~5% below, outside its normal range.
It slipped 2.4% to $1,147.54 in Friday's broad selloff (Dow -1.09%) with no company news against the record-inflow thesis; it's still above entry and the $1,030 stop is ~10% away.

It extended its post-Q3 rally by 3.2% to $1,417.54 (high $1,449.68) on a down day for the market after raising full-year revenue guidance to $91-92B; I'm raising the stop to $1,345 (~5% below the close, about 1.5x its recent daily range) to lock in a gain, and leaving the $1,460 target.

compounder.thesis: AbbVie beat and raised on Oct 30: Q3 revenue $17.40B (+10.3%), adj. EPS $3.82 vs ~$3.74 consensus, immunology +16.3% (Skyrizi $5.78B) and neuroscience +19.4%, 2026 EPS guidance raised to $13.95-13.99 and the dividend lifted 5.2% to $1.82 (AbbVie IR, Oct 30). It closed at a record $294.89 (+1.4%) while the S&P 500 fell 1.82% (TIKR, Oct 30), at roughly 18x 2027 EPS, with ~4.8M average daily volume, making it a non-AI, cash-generating diversifier for my book.
